status: Closed — validator usage telemetry and tier evidence are implemented and re-verified on 2026-09-06
finding: ATM validation surfaces can grow monotonically and make common flows slower because validators do not yet emit enough per-validator usage, latency, trigger-rate, failure-rate, and defect-interception counters to justify their placement in fast, default, full, or archive tiers.
expectedBehavior: Every validation unit should emit lightweight instrument-mode counters: validator id, mode tier, invocation count, skipped count, duration, failure count, blocking count, downstream defect/incident link when known, and task/surface context. Fast/default/full placement should be evidence-driven. Rarely used or expensive validators should move to full; never-used or no-impact validators should be archived or sampled.
evidenceOrRepro: Current executor output is instrumented through `createValidatorUsageTelemetry` and `buildValidatorLifecycleSummary`, emitting `atm.validatorUsageTelemetry.v1` with validator identity/version, tier, invocation/skipped/cache counters, duration, blocking count, fan-out, decision usage, and archive candidates. `node --strip-types scripts/validate-gate-telemetry-coverage.ts --json` exited 0 and `node --strip-types tests/cli/validator-dag-shared-cache.test.ts` exited 0 on 2026-09-06.
followUp: Keep `validator-dag-shared-cache.test.ts` and the telemetry coverage validator green. Tier changes and archive decisions remain owner-reviewed operational work; a new failure to emit per-validator telemetry should open a successor card.
